# @simular-ai/box

The command-line client for [box by Simular](https://box.simular.ai). box gives your AI agent a computer of its own: a cloud Linux desktop with Chrome and a shell, driven over MCP.

```sh
npx -y @simular-ai/box connect     # add box to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more
npx -y @simular-ai/box doctor      # check that box is set up right
npx -y @simular-ai/box --help
```

## Install

Run it without installing:

```sh
npx -y @simular-ai/box <command>
```

Or install it globally. The command is `simular-box` (`box` belongs to box.com's CLI):

```sh
npm i -g @simular-ai/box
simular-box connect
```

The package is a native binary. npm installs only the one for your machine, from one of these packages:

| OS | x64 | arm64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS | `@simular-ai/box-darwin-x64` | `@simular-ai/box-darwin-arm64` |
| Linux | `@simular-ai/box-linux-x64` | `@simular-ai/box-linux-arm64` |
| Windows | `@simular-ai/box-win32-x64` | `@simular-ai/box-win32-arm64` |

The launcher needs Node.js 18.17 or later. Don't install with `--omit=optional` (or `--no-optional`): the binary comes in as an optional dependency.

## Connect box to your AI apps

```sh
simular-box connect
```

`connect` finds the AI apps on this computer, asks which ones should use box, and adds the box MCP server (`https://mcp.box.simular.ai/mcp`) to each one in its own format. Other servers and settings in those files are left alone, each changed file gets a backup next to it (`*.box-backup-<time>`), and running it again changes nothing.

```sh
simular-box doctor     # is box set up right in each app? is the endpoint up? is the key valid?
simular-box remove     # undo connect
```

| App | `--client` | Where box goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | the `simular-box@simular-box` plugin (box server and skill), through `claude plugin install`; with `BOX_MCP_URL` set, a plain server through `claude mcp add` |
| Codex | `codex` | `[mcp_servers.box]` in `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` (default `~/.codex`) |
| Cursor | `cursor` | `mcpServers.box` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-cli` | `mcpServers.box` in `~/.gemini/settings.json` |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | `mcp.box` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` |
| Hermes Agent | `hermes` | `mcp_servers.box` in `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` (default `~/.hermes`) |
| OpenClaw | `openclaw` | through `openclaw mcp set box …` |
| VS Code | `vscode` | `servers.box` in the user `mcp.json` |
| Claude Desktop | `claude-desktop` | nothing is written: remote servers are connectors in the app, so connect prints the steps |

- Every app signs in to box with OAuth: the app opens a browser page, you sign in and click Approve. No key to copy.
- `--client cursor,codex --yes` picks apps without prompts; `--yes` alone picks every app found. `--dry-run` shows what would change.
- For always-on Hermes or OpenClaw servers, `--auth key` uses a personal key (from `BOX_TOKEN` or a hidden prompt, never an argument) instead of OAuth.
- connect only changes or removes a server that points at box by Simular. If an app already has a different server named `box` (such as box.com's), connect leaves that app unchanged and says so; add box next to it with `--name simular-box`.
- `doctor` checks, for each app: box is configured with the current URL, the endpoint answers and its sign-in metadata names the same URL, and a configured personal key is accepted. It prints a fix for each problem and exits 1 when something needs fixing. OAuth sign-ins are stored by each app, so doctor can't see those.

## Commands

Most commands take `--json` (machine-readable output) and `--help`. A box is named by its name or id: as the `[BOX]` argument where the examples show one, else with `--box` (`exec`, `rsh`, `snapshots`, `restore`, `offload`, `back`). Without one, commands use your first box.

### Sign in

```sh
simular-box login                  # sign this computer in, in the browser
simular-box login --token -        # or paste a personal key (cb_...) from stdin or a hidden prompt
simular-box auth status            # signed in, and how
simular-box logout                 # revoke this computer's device token and forget it
simular-box devices                # the computers and keys signed in to your account
simular-box devices revoke dev_…   # sign one of them out
```

`BOX_TOKEN=cb_...` (a personal key, for CI or a server) wins over a stored sign-in. A token is never accepted as an argument or printed.

### Your boxes

```sh
simular-box ls                     # list your boxes
simular-box wake [BOX]             # wake (or start) a box and wait until it runs
simular-box sleep [BOX]            # sleep; programs and memory come back on the next wake
simular-box create NAME            # another box
simular-box rename [BOX] NEW_NAME
simular-box delete [BOX]           # with its saved state and snapshots (asks first)
simular-box upgrade [BOX]          # move to the latest image; running programs restart (asks first)
simular-box usage                  # model usage today and this month, with your daily cap
simular-box watch                  # follow your boxes' changes live (--events: a box agent's events)
simular-box schedule set --cron "0 9 * * 1-5" [BOX]   # wake at set times (also: schedule list, schedule clear)
```

### Saves and snapshots

```sh
simular-box save [BOX]                       # save files, sign-ins and agent history now
simular-box snapshots                        # a box's kept snapshots, newest first
simular-box snapshots browse latest ~/Documents
simular-box snapshots search latest report
simular-box snapshots changes latest         # what changed since the save before it
simular-box restore latest ~/Documents/a.txt # copied into ~/Restored/<save time>/ in the box
```

### Run commands in a box

```sh
simular-box exec -- uname -a                 # run a command; exits with its code
simular-box exec -c 'ls ~ | wc -l'           # a shell command line (bash -lc in the box)
simular-box exec -t -- bash                  # on a terminal
simular-box rsh [--box NAME] COMMAND...      # ssh-style remote shell, for rsync -e and GIT_SSH_COMMAND (no --help)
```

### Sign in to a site in the box

```sh
simular-box fill --origin https://accounts.google.com -u me@example.com --submit
```

`fill` fills the sign-in form in the box's browser. The password (or, with `--code`, a one-time code) is read from a hidden prompt or stdin, never from arguments. `--show` only shows which site the box's browser has open.

### Move a coding task into your box: offload and back

```sh
simular-box offload install-cli --kind claude    # once per box: the vendor's official installer
simular-box offload sign-in --kind claude        # once per box: that CLI's own login, run in the box
simular-box offload --kind claude                # copy this repo into the box; an agent there continues from your hand-over
simular-box offload inbox                        # what the box agent posted (answer with: offload send "...")
simular-box back                                 # wait for its hand-over, fetch its commits, merge them here
```

`--kind` is `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`. In Claude Code with the simular-box plugin, `/simular-box:offload` and `/simular-box:back` do this for you. Elsewhere, write the hand-over to the path `offload handover-path` prints, or paste the request `offload --handover-prompt` prints into your agent. `back` lands the box's commits as a fast-forward when your repo has not changed, else as a clean merge applied uncommitted, else on a branch `box/back-<time>` with your work tree untouched. Offload needs a git repo, `git` and `rsync`.

Offload copies what git tracks (committed files and the index's entries, with their uncommitted changes) and the repo's history. Untracked and git-ignored files stay on this computer; stage a new file with `git add` to take it, and opt a secret in with `offload secrets add`.

### Traffic exit and home egress

```sh
simular-box exit [BOX] [direct|residential|home|default]   # show or set where a box's traffic leaves from
simular-box residential [on|off]                            # your account's residential exit default
simular-box daemon install       # the background daemon, started at login (also: status, logs, stop, uninstall)
simular-box proxy enable         # lend this computer's connection to your boxes (runs in the daemon)
simular-box proxy status         # link state, counters, recent destinations
simular-box proxy disable
```

`proxy enable` asks you to type a code shown in a dialog on this computer's screen, so it needs a terminal.

### Other

```sh
simular-box version                # or --version
simular-box --endpoint URL ls      # another box endpoint for one command (also BOX_ENDPOINT)
```

`BOX_MCP_URL` changes the MCP URL that `connect` and `doctor` use (for example staging), and the endpoint of the other commands when `BOX_ENDPOINT` is not set. Sign-ins are kept in `~/.simular-box/` (`BOX_HOME` moves it).

## Platform notes

- **Windows:** `offload` and `back` are not supported yet (they copy the repo with rsync) and exit 3. The other `offload` subcommands and everything else work.
- **Where the token lives:** in the macOS Keychain and Windows Credential Manager; on Linux, in `~/.simular-box/credentials.json` (`0600`).

## Upgrading from 0.x (the JavaScript CLI)

1.0 replaces the JavaScript CLI under the same package name and the same `simular-box` command. What changes:

- A native binary instead of a Node.js program, with many new commands: everything above beyond `connect`, `doctor`, `remove`, `login`, `logout`, `rsh` and `offload` / `back`.
- Fixed exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage error or cancelled, 3 blocked by a precondition, 4 needs sign-in, 5 needs confirmation (rerun with `--yes`; offload used 4 for this before). `rsh` and `exec` exit with the remote command's code, or 255.
- The license: 1.0 and later are proprietary (see below).

What stays: your app configs (connect leaves an up-to-date box entry from 0.x as it is) and your sign-in in `~/.simular-box/credentials.json`. An offload started with 0.x can be brought back with 1.0. On macOS and Windows, 1.0 moves the token from that file into the Keychain or Credential Manager the first time it reads it.

To go back to the JavaScript CLI:

```sh
npx @simular-ai/box@0.2.0 <command>
```

On macOS and Windows, run `npx @simular-ai/box@0.2.0 login` once first: 0.2.0 reads the token only from the file, so it sees a sign-in that 1.0 moved as signed out.
